newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soymeal exporters sign deals, prices strong.
newsitem.headline: Indian soymeal exporters sign deals, prices strong.

text.p: Indian soymeal exporters are signing fresh contracts at high prices following brisk export demand, traders said on Tuesday.
Importers were booking orders on fears that lower soymeal availability from India in the 1996/97 (Nov-Oct) season might further boost prices, they added.
Prices for November-December shipments were buoyant at $261-262 per tonne, against $188-189 at the same time last year.
Contracts for soymeal yellow for the new season started from $238 per tonne FAS (free alongside ship).
Traders said exporters, who had been hesitant about entering into fresh business, started signing deals because of attractive price offers.
"Around 100,000 tonnes of soymeal have been contracted for the new season to date," said a trader. Export contracts for 200,000 tonnes of soymeal were signed at this time last year.
Industry officials said India's soymeal exports in 1995/96 were expected to be around 2.6 million tonnes, up on an earlier estimate of 2.4 million.
No estimates of soymeal exports for 1996/97 have been made.

The industry set a goal of 4.5 million tonnes for soybean production in 1996/97 when sowing began in July, but traders expect output to be 20 percent below target due to erratic weather in growing areas.
India is expected to produce 4.45 million tonnes of soybeans in 1995/96.
Traders said Indian soybean and soymeal prices in the current 1995/96 season have reached record highs due to limited availability.
They said daily soybean arrivals had dwindled to 300 tonnes per day compared with 20,000 tonnes in the peak four-month period starting from November 1995.
"There is hardly 45,000 tonnes soybean with the farmers and around 30,000 tonnes soybean with the processing plants and mediators," said a trader.
In central Indian markets spot soybeans were quoted at 12,700-13,100 rupees per tonne against 10,000-10,100 at the same time last year and 9,300-9,400 at the start of the season in November.
Soymeal yellow was quoted at $276-277 per tonne FAS against $200-201 at the same time last year and $185-188 in November.
"Due to extremly low availability of soybean most processing plants have already stopped functioning," said a trader.
